preconditions.description: The number of characters n must be between 3 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of known relationships m must be between 0 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(a) <= n and 1 <= int(b) <= n and a != b and c in {0, 1} for a, b, c in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: Each relationship must involve two distinct characters labeled from 1 to n, and c_i must be either 0 (hate) or 1 (love).

preconditions.expression: len({(a, b) for a, b, c in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) if a < b}) == len({(a, b) for a, b, c in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])})
preconditions.description: Each pair of characters is described at most once in the input.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer modulo 1,000,000,007.
The output is a valid count modulo 1,000,000,007.

The output represents the number of valid ways to fill in the remaining relationships such that for every triplet of characters (A, B, C), exactly one pair loves each other and the other two hate each other, or all three pairs love each other.
